v1.23.0 is the release where the companies in one group can differ. A corporate parent can own
LLCs and partnerships and the group's statements still read as one; one company's books can be
kept in QuickBooks while another's are kept here; and a public filer that moved to a new
registrant keeps its history under its ticker. Around that, a distribution from an equity-method
investee is an operating cash flow, and the graph tier, the token path and the instance roles are
tightened.

Covers everything since v1.22.10; the 1.22.x patches carried generated changelogs.

## Groups of more than one form

**The consolidation entity has no Style of its own.** Its books hold the group's adjustments, so
its statements are read under the group parent's Reporting Style everywhere: the live statement,
filed reports, the close stamp and the export bundle. It takes the parent's Style when it is
created or retyped, follows the parent's through `change-reporting-style`, and cannot be given
another (the operation answers 422 on it). A Style left on an existing consolidation entity's row
is no longer read, so no migration is needed.

**Eliminations carry the members' own cash flow rows.** An operating company's lines carry only
the rows its own cash flow presents, as before. The consolidation entity's lines carry any row
some company of the group presents, so an elimination of an LLC member's contribution is tagged
with the members' contribution row under a corporate parent rather than posted untagged. The
`flowCandidates` read offers the consolidation entity the same set.

**A group read places a flow the parent's Style has no row for.** An investing or financing flow
of a member in another form takes a row under its section in the combined and consolidated cash
flow, so a member's contribution and the elimination that offsets it meet on one line. This holds
on the live statement; a stored statement does not yet place it.

## Where each company's books are kept

**The write policy belongs to one company's books.** A connection now records the entity it is
for (`entity_id`) and whether it is that entity's ledger of record (`keeps_books`, new on
`ConnectionResponse`). Every policy question is asked about an entity and answered by the
connection that keeps its books: whether its close writes back or shadows, where its drafts would
publish, whether its sync is current, and whether a bank feed may book there. A subsidiary with no
such connection keeps its books here, whatever the parent's connection says, and its journal no
longer behaves as if QuickBooks kept them.

- A connection becomes the keeper when it finishes authorizing; a later authorization for the same
  entity takes over from it.
- `execute-event-block` publishes only to the connection that keeps the event's own entity's books.
- `set-write-policy` refuses a connection that keeps no books, and write-back on a ledger nothing
  can be written to.
- QuickBooks still keeps the group parent's books only.

## Cash flow

**A distribution from an equity-method investee is operating.** Cash received against the
investment lands on its own operating row,
`EquityMethodInvestmentDividendsOrDistributions`, beside the share of income it follows, rather
than reading as a sale of the investment in investing (ASC 230-10-45-21D). A distribution past the
investor's share of earnings is a return of the investment: tag the cash line
`ProceedsFromEquityMethodInvestmentDividendsOrDistributionsReturnOfCapital` and it is presented in
investing. A sale of the investment is tagged with the sale row. A posted distribution moves to
operating on the next read of an open period; a closed month keeps what it stamped.

The engine's flows are now every concept with an activity, operating included, from one shared
definition, and `FlowCandidate.activity` can be `operating`.

## SEC

**A ticker keeps its history when the company changes registrant.** A holding-company
reorganization or a redomicile moves a company to a new CIK under the same ticker, and EDGAR links
the two only in the successor's Form 8-K12B. A curated table now records each such succession with
the filing that states it, and each unrelated takeover of a symbol. A successor's catalog file
lists its predecessors' filings with its own (each entry names the CIK that filed it), and the
graph puts the ticker on both registrants, so `XOM` reads Exxon Mobil Corp's annual reports again.
A filer whose symbol went to an unrelated company gives it up, EDGAR's current holder owns a
contested ticker, and a takeover with neither finding on record is reported by every catalog run.

## Graph tier

- **A graph delete removes every file the graph owns on disk.**
- **Pool maintenance takes database locks without the global lock**, so it can no longer wait on a
  graph that a rebuild holds while blocking every other graph on the instance.
- **Shared replicas are refreshed from Dagster only.** Service Refresh no longer offers
  `shared-replicas` or `all`; a replica takes a release at the next instance refresh.

## Security

- Token-path writes commit as one transaction.
- The graph instance roles reach only the two secrets a graph instance uses.

## Infrastructure

- Migrations run on the orchestrator's boot: on the platform database, the connection's entity and
  keeper columns, backfilled for existing QuickBooks connections; on the extensions database, the
  equity-method distribution and return-of-capital rows, in the library and every tenant.
- The tenant keep-set admits the two equity-method cash flow concepts.
- The reporting acceptance harness reads an operating row that is an investment's default from the
  journal lines, as it reads investing.
- The lock carries `robosystems-client` 2.38.0, which has `keeps_books` on a connection.

A deployment on v1.22.10 restarts into this release with no manual step. The graph instance role
change applies as the stacks update, and needs every graph container on v1.22.9 or later; a
container on an older image reads other secrets at boot.
